findings.issue: On Windows, Path.write_text translates the checksum line ending to CRLF. Git Bash sha256sum -c treats the trailing carriage return as part of the archive filename and fails to verify a valid archive. The existing read_text assertion normalizes line endings and misses this; write an LF-only checksum and assert its raw bytes.

needs-human: Issue #6 still lacks a recorded owner decision of SOURCE_ONLY or DISTRIBUTED_BINARY and clean-machine evidence for the chosen path. The PR correctly discloses these gaps, but CI and fixture archive tests do not fulfill the issue's source-build or Windows download/launch/sidecar acceptance.

summary: Fixed the Windows SHA-256 CRLF defect with a byte-level regression: red reproduced, then all 3 release-contract tests and real Git Bash sha256sum verification passed. needs-human: record SOURCE_ONLY or DISTRIBUTED_BINARY and complete the selected clean-machine acceptance before closing #6. Broader suite limitations are recorded in .issue-loop-evidence.json; no push or release was performed.
